main_text.head: AD CAP. XI.
main_text.p: Pag. 102. lin. 9. & 10. Πεϱιαχ-ϑεὶς κύκλῳ τᾶ ἀμφιθιάτρες.] Id di-cunt Circumduci; sicut Traduci, cùm ostentui dumtaxat per ora populi ducebantur, & sæpe alibi puniendi. Suetonius in Tito, cap. vii. Hos (Delatores) novis-sime traductos per amphitheatri are-nam, partim subjici in servos ac va-nire præcepit, partim in asperrimas insularum avehi. Nescio an Mar-tialis versus, qui jamdiu cubat in morbo, sic sanandus, lib 1. de his ipsis Delatoribus & Titi facto:

l.i: Turba gravis paci placidaque inimica quieti,
Traducta est titulis, nec cepit arena nocentes,
Et delator habet quod dabat exsilium.

page.notes: The Greek in the Pag. 102 reference is partly illegible in the scan; transcribed as best possible. Text on the page ends with a hyphenated word "Titu-" continuing on the next page. Line "Quæ semper" has an underlined "Quæ" in the original.
